elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Renewal remains automatic ("This Agreement will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms") and no mutual-written-agreement renewal was substituted, so this element depends on all conditional automatic-renewal elements being satisfied; the 30-day opt-out and 60-day reminder elements are not satisfied, so the excusing condition fails.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Retained text: "automatically renew for additional 1-year terms" — 12-month renewal terms, not multi-year.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Inserted language requires notice "at least 60 days prior to the end of the then-current term"; 60 > 30. To reach preferred, change the inserted figure to 30 days.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation appears in the rendered clause; only the margin comment mentions the preferred position. A Kubient obligation to notify Customer at least 60 days before each renewal date would need to be added in operative text.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: paragraph 4(a) renews on existing terms and contains no renewal price-increase or uplift mechanic (fees are the revenue share set in the Exhibit), so no cap is triggered.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Inserted operative text: "unless Customer gives written notice of non-renewal at least 60 days prior to the end of the then-current term" — a Customer-only non-renewal right with a 60-day window, satisfying the ≤60-day fallback. The deterministic check reporting "number not found" is a pattern-matching artefact (the clause uses the bare numeral "60 days" rather than a spelled-out "sixty (60)" form); on substance the window is 60 days.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: renewal continues on the existing terms with no price-increase or escalation language in paragraph 4(a) or the renewal mechanic, so no uplift cap is required.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the single insertion supplies a Customer non-renewal right on 60 days' notice tied to the end of the then-current term, and the price-cap element is untriggered because renewal is on existing terms.

Preferred is not reached: the opt-out window is 60 days rather than 30, and no Vendor reminder obligation (at least 60 days before renewal) appears in operative language — the reminder is only referenced in the margin comment, which does not count.

Minimal: the edit adds one clause inside the existing renewal sentence and deletes nothing; the 90-day mutual for-any-reason termination right, the Initial-Term restriction, the fees-during-termination allocation and the 4(b) breach/insolvency rights are all retained verbatim. No survival tails, procedures or extra requirements were added.

Intent preserved: non-renewal at natural term end is distinct from the mid-term termination rights, so the retained sentence "Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit" does not contradict a notice of non-renewal delivered before the Initial Term expires; no undefined terms or dangling cross-references are created (the "Term" definition still keys off the renewal sentence).

Drafting note if the preferred position is pursued: replace "at least 60 days" with "at least 30 days" and add an express Kubient obligation to notify Customer of the upcoming renewal at least 60 days before the end of the then-current term.
